<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par126 />''the sixth''; but {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם שֵׁנִי|translate=a second day}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=8}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם הָֽרִאשֹׁן|translate=from the first day onward}} (not before {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=10|verse=12}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=18}} is {{GHGheb|text=מִן־הַיּוֹם הָֽרִאשׁוֹן}} used instead of it). On the other hand, the article is ''always'' found after {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, hence {{GHGheb|text=בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי}}, &c., although it is possible that the original reading in these cases was {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}}, and that the article is only due to the Masora. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=25}} the text is evidently corrupt (see verse 26).—Especially also in certain frequently recurring combinations as in particularizing the gates in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=2}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=10}}, and courts in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=7|verse=8}}, 12, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=28}}; and very often when the attribute consists of a participle, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=16|hidebook=1}} {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫רֶב הַיּוֹנָה|translate=the sword which oppresses}} (''?''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=14|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=2}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} (''the impenetrable forest?'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=21}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|x}}
Of the other examples, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=29}} (where, however, the Samaritan reads {{GHGheb|text=הכבשות}}), 41:26 (but cf. verse 4), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=17}} may at any rate be explained on the ground that the preceding cardinal number is equivalent to a determinant; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=28|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, 10, &c., the substantive is already determined by {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=29}} ({{GHGheb|text=דְּבַשׁ}}) by {{GHGheb|text=מְעַט}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=20}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=הַשְּׂכִירָה}} might also be understood as a subsequent explanation of {{GHGheb|text=בְּתַ֫עַר}}) and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=35}}, the omission of the article after the preposition is certainly due merely to the Masora. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=23}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים}} is to be read twice), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=4|verse=7}} (where however {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּ הָהָר}} is probably meant), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=18}} (where a {{GHGheb|text=ה}} precedes {{GHGheb|text=הָרִים}}, hence probably a case of haplography), the omission of the article before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=ר}} (?) and {{GHGheb|text=ה}} may be due to a regard for euphony (see ''z'' below). On the other hand, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=18}} (read {{GHGheb|text=הָאֶ֫בֶן הַגְּ׳}}), 17:12 ({{GHGheb|text=הַזֶּה}} is a later addition), 19:22 (cf. the LXX), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=3|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=2|verse=3}} (read {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹי}} or omit {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹיִם}} with Cornill), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=4}}, either the text is corrupt, or the expression incorrect. But in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=7|verse=10}} acc. to D. H. Müller (''Anzeiger der Wiener Akad.'', phil-hist. Kl. 1902, no. x) {{GHGheb|text=הַטּוֹב}} is the genitive of a substantive, ''aromatic oil, sweet cane'' (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=20}} read {{GHGheb|text=וּקְנֵה}}), ''like spiced wine''. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=39|verse=2}} read {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫מֶן הַטּוֹב}} and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=133|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=כְּשֶׁ֫מֶן חַטּ׳}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|126|y}}
(''b'') No article with the attribute, while the substantive is determined either by the article, or a suffix, or a following genitive. Thus the article is sometimes omitted with demonstratives, since they are already to a certain extent determined by their meaning (cf. also the ''Mêšaʿ'' inscription, l. 3, {{GHGheb|text=הבמת זאת|translate=this high place}}); as with {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=33}} (evidently for euphony, and so probably often); 30:16, 32:23, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=10}}; with {{GHGheb|text=הִיא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=21}}; with {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=8}} (according to the Masora {{GHGheb|text=זוּ}} is a relative pronoun here, as always elsewhere); with {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=23}}, according to the present corrupt text (the original reading {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עַם יהוה}} became {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־עַם אֱלֹהִים}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} was then corrupted to {{GHGheb|text=אֵלֶּה}}); so, almost without exception, when the substantive is determined only by a suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=1|verse=2}} and 8:8 f., where {{GHGheb|text=חלי}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=19}}, has arisen by contraction from {{GHGheb|text=חָלְיִי}}, or we should simply read {{GHGheb|text=חָלְיִ}} (in all these passages with {{GHGheb|text=זֶה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=8}} (with {{GHGheb|text=זֹאת}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=21}} (with {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫לֶּה}}).

The article is sometimes omitted also with the attributes referring to proper names,<ref>Cf. Nöldeke, ''Beiträge zur semit. Sprachwiss.'', p. 48, n. 1.</ref> as {{GHGheb|text=צִידוֹן רַבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=11|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=19|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲמָת רַבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=2}}. Other examples are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=16|verse=3}}, 5, 18:13, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=17}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=7|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=8|verse=5}} with the article). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=11}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=תְּהוֹם רַבָּה}} is also a case of this kind, {{GHGheb|text=תְּהוֹם}} being used (almost always without the article) as a sort of proper name; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֵל עֶלְיוֹן|translate=the most high}}<section end=par126 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
